the following question: How can we combine the advantages of RNNs with the advantages of CRFs to produce an even better language understanding model?

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RNNs can be used to build a state-of-the-art language understanding system.
the RNN tagger is a good tagger and the CRF tagger is a better tagger, but they are not comparable in the sense that they are solving different problems.
the RNN tagger with CRF-like features outperforms the CRF tagger by 2% absolute on the ATIS dataset and the RNN taggers outperform the CRF taggers on all web search datasets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a new language understanding model which combines the advantages of RNN and CRF, and we show that it can achieve better results than the state-of-the-art language understanding models.
we have demonstrated that the RNN can be used as a powerful language modeling tool, but that it can be further improved with ideas from the CRF model.
we have shown that RNNs can be used to model label dependencies and achieve better performance than CRFs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of a recurrent network can be significantly enhanced by explicitly modeling output label dependencies and by using offline decoding.
RNNs are not a replacement for CRFs, rather they are a powerful extension of them.
combining elements of CRFs with RNNs is a fruitful approach for language understanding.
